chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

To one of his sons: 'Did you walk briskly in the valley of Muhassar?' He said, 'No.' So he ordered him to return until he walked briskly. His son said to him, 'I do not know it.' So he said to him, 'Ask the people.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam instruct his son to do regarding the valley of Muhassar?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the specific ritual of performing *sa'y* (brisk walking) in the valley of Muhassar, a practice rooted in the traditions of the Ahl al-Bayt. When the Imam’s son was unfamiliar with the location, the directive to 'ask the people' underscores the reliance on communal knowledge and scholarly transmission to preserve the precise details of these devotional acts.
